subject: BYM2 model - logProb is NA or NaN

messages.author: c4b09b129d99cc26
messages.subject: BYM2 model - logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi all,

I'm fitting a BYM2 model (Riebler et al., 2016)* in Nimble. However, I keep getting warning "logProb is NA or NaN" even though I don't have missing values in data. Could anyone  suggest what might be the reason?

I attached my code and a simulated dataset for reproduction of my issue.
Thank very much in advance!

Best regards,
Hanah.

---

(*) Riebler, A., Sørbye, S. H., Simpson, D., & Rue, H. (2016). An intuitive Bayesian spatial model for disease mapping that accounts for scaling. Statistical methods in medical research, 25(4), 1145-1165.

messages.author: 7878556d408ec9ec
messages.subject: Re: BYM2 model - logProb is NA or NaN
parts:
Hi Hanah,

It seems like you do not provide the value of 'scale' as a constant to the model (you calculated it but did not provide it in the nb.const list). In the model, 'scale' has a value of NA and causes NA values for mu and the message you saw.  It is useful to check using model$calculate(nodes) when you get NA/NaN issues to see which nodes caused the issue. This makes error tracking easier. Hope it helps. 

Best wishes,
Wei
